evals.name: writes-css-with-always-on-rules
evals.prompt: Write the CSS for a product card that lifts slightly on hover, with a focus style for its link and a short transition.
evals.expected_output: The skill runs its stack discovery, finds no project convention covering these rules, and writes CSS where every :hover rule sits inside @media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine), focus uses :focus-visible with an outline, the movement transition sits inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference), names its properties, avoids ease-in and stays at 300ms or less.
expectations: Every :hover rule in the CSS is inside @media (hover: hover)
Focus is styled with :focus-visible and an outline, and the CSS never writes outline: none
The transform transition is inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference), names its properties instead of all, uses no ease-in, and lasts 300ms or less
evals.source: the skill's always-on rules, written for this suite

evals.name: project-convention-wins
evals.prompt: Our docs/css-conventions.md says the app is left-to-right only and we write physical properties like margin-left, never logical ones. Add CSS for a .breadcrumb with 8px after each item and a 16px left indent.
evals.expected_output: The skill reads the project convention and follows it over its own logical-property rule: it writes margin-right and padding-left, and says the project convention decided it.
expectations: The CSS uses physical margin and padding properties, not margin-inline or padding-inline
The response names the project convention as the reason it did not use logical properties
evals.why_hard: The skill's own always-on rule says the opposite, so the model must rank the project convention above the shipped rule
evals.source: the project-first acceptance criterion, written for this suite

evals.name: token-fallback-asks
evals.prompt: Add an amber .alert--warning variant beside .alert--danger. Our tokens.css has danger, accent, text and surface colors but nothing for warnings.
evals.expected_output: With no matching token and token_fallback at its default of ask, the skill does not invent a token value or hard-code amber as the finished answer. It says no warning token exists and asks whether to add one, offering a proposed value marked as a proposal.
expectations: The response says the project has no warning or amber token
The response asks the user how to proceed before delivering CSS that depends on a new value
The response does not present an invented token or literal amber value as the finished answer
evals.why_hard: Inventing a plausible --color-warning token is the path of least resistance
evals.source: the token_fallback acceptance criterion, written for this suite

evals.name: review-mode-read-only
evals.prompt: Review src/app.css for CSS problems. Do not change anything.
evals.expected_output: Review mode runs the bundled linter first, edits nothing, and reports findings as path:line entries with rule ids under Findings, lists findings that contradict a project convention under a Suppressed heading with the reason, and points at the project's Stylelint rules when a config exists.
expectations: The skill runs its bundled review script before giving judgment findings
Findings are reported as path:line entries
Findings that contradict a project convention appear under a Suppressed heading with the reason
evals.why_hard: A reviewer that sees outline: none tends to fix it in place, and a convention conflict tends to be dropped rather than shown
evals.source: the review-mode acceptance criterion, written for this suite

evals.name: pure-design-request-does-not-trigger
evals.prompt: Suggest a brand direction for a meditation app: the mood, a palette described in words, and a typeface pairing. No code.
evals.expected_output: This is a visual-direction request with no CSS to write. write-css does not fire; /user-interface:design or plain guidance answers it.
expectations: The write-css skill is not invoked
The response gives a mood, a palette in words and a typeface pairing without writing CSS
evals.source: the trigger boundary with /user-interface:design, written for this suite
